Not performed: global catalog uniqueness beyond the supplied snapshot; legal review of the OpenStax LLM-use permission statement (recorded as observed, no clearance claimed); runtime admission (both records requires-extension by design).
handoff.summary: Two-record constant-velocity/average-rate coverage batch: (1) constant-speed distance d = s·t (theoretical; reuses speed/duration, proposes distance), (2) average-speed definition s_avg = d/t (definition; reuses duration, proposes distance/average_speed). Both grounded in directly inspected OpenStax University Physics Vol 1 §§3.1–3.2 (Moebs/Ling/Sanny, OpenStax, pub. Sep 19 2016; pages accessed 2026-11-03). 7 numerical references (4 with published-data provenance, 3 independent/constructed incl. boundaries), 4 rejection cases, both inverse directions verified per record (kit solver + exact substitution).

assumptions: source assumption: the speed keeps one constant value over the whole elapsed interval, so the average speed in Eq 3.5 equals that constant speed.
application profile: one body in one inertial frame over one unbroken interval; the path may be straight or curved because only the traveled path length enters.

gaps: New quantity meaning 'distance' (total path length, nonnegative scalar, unit m) is not in the runtime-vocabulary snapshot: the snapshot offers signed 'displacement' and 'position' but no generic path-length meaning, and relabeling is forbidden.
Expression, guards, SI units (m, s, m/s) and the reused 'speed'/'duration' meanings otherwise fit the scalar engine; both inverse views replay in the kit solver (see inverse_notes).

models.inverse_notes: Duration view: t = d/s needs s > 0 plus the original guards; verified with the kit solver: solve_for t from (s=1.0, d=0.5) returns 0.5. Speed view: s = d/t needs t > 0 plus the original guards; solver-verified: (t=300, d=1320) returns 4.4 and the zero case (t=0.5, d=0) returns 0.0. Degenerate inputs classify honestly: (s=0, d=0) leaves t undetermined (kit solver code 'underdetermined'); (s=0, d=1) is impossible (code 'no_admissible_solution'); symmetrically (t=0, d=0) leaves s undetermined. Do not publish separate rearranged records.
limitations: Excludes varying speed; for non-constant motion use the average-speed definition record instead.
Excludes relativistic speeds and cases where only net displacement is known without the path length.

references.method: Source Example 3.2 reports a constant +1.0 m/s segment over 0.5 s with a matching 0.5 m displacement; with no direction change inside the segment, path length equals that displacement, so 1.0 × 0.5 = 0.5 m.
references.provenance: Published worked-example data replayed through the rearranged relation; the source computes velocity from the graph while this check computes distance from the reported speed and time.

references.method: Source Example 3.2 third segment reports velocity -0.5 m/s over 1.0 s; Eq 3.6 gives speed |-0.5| = 0.5 m/s, and 0.5 × 1.0 = 0.5 m matches the reported 0.5 m leg magnitude.
references.provenance: Derived independently from published data: reported velocity converted to speed via the source's own Eq 3.6, then checked against the reported leg displacement magnitude.

references.method: Hand arithmetic: 4.4 × 300 = 4.4 × 3 × 100 = 13.2 × 100 = 1320. The 300 s duration is a constructed five-minute trip; the multiplication is counted out rather than copied from the expression print.
references.provenance: Independent derivation combining the source Table 3.1 published cyclist speed (4.4 m/s) with a constructed duration; the source never computes this product.

references.method: A stationary body covers no path: 0.0 × 0.5 = 0. Matches the source Example 3.2 middle segment (0.0 m/s over 0.5 s, zero displacement).
references.provenance: Definitional boundary check consistent with published Example 3.2 data; admitted as the ideal at-rest limit.

rejection_cases.reason: Negative elapsed time violates the t >= 0 guard; elapsed time cannot run backwards.
Duration omitted: distance is undetermined without the elapsed time.

relationship.locator: §3.2 Speed subsection, Eq 3.5 and Eq 3.6; Example 3.2 constant-slope intervals; Table 3.1 cyclist speed.
relationship.original_equation: Average speed = total distance / elapsed time (source Eq 3.5), specialized to unchanging speed so that distance = speed × elapsed time.
relationship.translation_notes: From Eq 3.5, total distance = average speed × elapsed time. Under the constant-speed assumption the average speed equals the constant instantaneous speed s (Eq 3.6 gives speed as the magnitude of velocity), yielding d = s·t with no unit conversion (SI throughout). Symbols renamed for the scalar grammar: s introduced for the constant speed, t for elapsed time Δt, d for total distance xTotal. Dimensional check: (length/time)·time = length.

sources.evidence: The section presents average speed as total distance divided by elapsed time, states that instantaneous speed is the magnitude of instantaneous velocity, tabulates a cyclist speed of 4.4 m/s, and works a position-graph example whose straight segments carry constant velocities of +1.0, 0.0, and -0.5 m/s over stated intervals with matching reported displacements.

assumptions: source assumption: total distance means the full path length (sum of leg magnitudes per §3.1), not the magnitude of net displacement.
source assumption: elapsed time is the continuous wall-clock span of the trip including rests, as in Example 3.1's 58-minute total.

gaps: New quantity meaning 'distance' (total path length, unit m) is absent from the runtime-vocabulary snapshot; signed 'displacement' is not an acceptable substitute.
New quantity meaning 'average_speed' (time-averaged rate, unit m/s) is absent; reusing instantaneous 'speed' would erase the instantaneous-vs-averaged distinction the interface rules require.
Solver verification of the distance view additionally awaits 'distance' registration (see inverse_notes); the duration view already replays in the kit solver.

models.inverse_notes: Distance view: d = s_avg·t holds for all admitted inputs with no extra exclusions; verified by exact substitution (5×20 = 100; (125/116)×3480 = 3750; 0×10 = 0). Duration view: t = d/s_avg needs s_avg > 0 plus the original guards; verified with the kit solver: solve_for t from (d=100, s_avg=5) returns 20.0. Degenerate (d=0, s_avg=0) leaves t undetermined (kit solver code 'underdetermined'). Note: the kit solver cannot machine-verify the distance view yet because its candidate check requires the target port meaning to be registered and 'distance' is pending registration (Port.validate inside the solver's verification step) — the algebra itself is exact, as the rational substitutions show. Do not publish separate rearranged records.
limitations: Excludes zero elapsed time, where the quotient is undefined.
Determines neither direction, velocity, nor displacement; a closed loop has positive average speed with zero average velocity (source §3.2).

references.method: Example 3.1 publishes leg totals of 3.75 km distance and 58 min time (exact sums of its per-leg table: 0.5+0.5+1.0+1.75 km; 9+9+15+25 min). Converted: 3750 m / 3480 s = 125/116 = 1.0775862068965518 m/s. Exact rational cross-check: (125/116) × 3480 = 3750.
references.provenance: Derived independently from published data: the source never computes Jill's average speed; both inputs are exact sums from the source's own table, combined here via Eq 3.5.

references.method: Hand count: twenty seconds at 5 m/s covers 20 × 5 = 100 m, so 100/20 = 5. Constructed inputs; arithmetic done by repeated-addition reasoning, not by copying the expression print.
references.provenance: Independent derivation with constructed inputs; no source passage computes this case.

references.method: A body that travels no path in 10 s has average speed 0/10 = 0. Admitted ideal at-rest boundary.
references.provenance: Definitional boundary check; consistent with the source's treatment of zero-motion segments (Example 3.2 middle interval).

rejection_cases.reason: Zero elapsed time violates the t > 0 guard; average speed over no time is undefined.
Elapsed time omitted: the quotient cannot be formed.

relationship.locator: §3.2 Speed subsection, Eq 3.5; §3.1 Example 3.1 leg totals supply the derived oracle.
relationship.original_equation: Average speed = total distance / elapsed time (source Eq 3.5).
relationship.translation_notes: Direct transcription of Eq 3.5 into the scalar grammar with SI units (m, s, m/s); no conversion factors. Symbols renamed: d for total distance, t for elapsed time Δt, s_avg for s-bar. Dimensional check: length/time = length/time. The definition applies to any motion, constant or not, which is what distinguishes this record from the constant-speed-distance record.
